title: Invisible in Search? Auditing Aesthetic Bias in the Visual Representation of Holocaust Victims on Google
findings: The study found that Google's visual representation of Holocaust victims, who were predominantly Jewish, deviates from traditional memorial aesthetics. Instead of focusing on women and children, Google's search results tend to propagate a male-dominated representation, with an emphasis on older men in the context of atrocities. This risks rendering gender-specific suffering invisible. Furthermore, the representation varies significantly across different geographic locations and languages (e.g., queries in Hebrew from Israel yielded substantively different results), suggesting that search algorithms produce their own aesthetic of victimhood depending on the search context.
